detail.title: Synthesis of Predictive Processing in Musical Experience
detail.summary: We synthesized existing research on musical beat perception and emotional engagement, specifically evaluating the Action Simulation for Auditory Prediction (ASAP) hypothesis and the interoceptive inference framework. Musical experience is framed as a dynamic predictive process where rhythmic structure and harmonic patterns modulate an observer's internal model, transforming auditory inputs into emotionally salient experiences. The dual evidence base supports a view of music as a form of controlled hallucination, linking temporal predictions to motor and autonomic responses. This work provides a foundation for examining individual differences in predictive processing capacity as a variable in musical appreciation.
